function_v0.doc: One-time bootstrap. The `admin` address must sign the init tx, which\ncloses the front-running window between deploy and first call.
function_v0.name: initialize

function_v0.doc: Add a new authorized writer. Caller must be in the auth set and sign.
function_v0.name: add_authorized

function_v0.doc: Remove an authorized writer. Caller must be in the auth set and sign.\nRefuses to empty the auth set so the contract never becomes orphaned.
function_v0.name: remove_authorized

function_v0.doc: Public read of the current authorized writer set.
function_v0.name: get_authorized

function_v0.doc: Record the SHA-256 hash for one stage of a gem. Append-only:\nre-setting an existing stage panics with `StageAlreadySet`. To correct\na mistake, deploy a new gem record under a new gemID.
function_v0.name: set_gem_hash

function_v0.doc: Record several stage hashes in one transaction. Each entry is subject\nto the same append-only and whitelist rules as `set_gem_hash`. If any\nentry violates a rule, the whole call reverts.
function_v0.name: set_gem_hashes

function_v0.doc:
Extend the storage TTL of a gem's on-chain record WITHOUT modifying it.

Persistent entries are archived once their TTL runs out, after which the
anchored hashes can't be read without a costly restore. Because the
contract is append-only, an existing stage can never be re-written to
piggy-back a TTL bump \xe2\x80\x94 so this dedicated keeper entrypoint is the only
way to keep a gem's provenance alive indefinitely.

Permissionless by design: extending TTL only prolongs storage (the
caller pays the fee) and can't alter or reveal anything, so anyone who
cares about a gem's longevity may keep it alive. No-op if the gem has no
record on-chain, so keepers can call it blindly over a batch of IDs.
function_v0.name: bump_gem_ttl

function_v0.doc: Read the recorded hash for one (gem, stage) pair. None if not set.
function_v0.name: get_gem_stage_hash

function_v0.doc: Read every stage hash recorded for a gem. None if the gem has no\nrecord on-chain at all.
function_v0.name: get_gem

function_v0.doc: Convenience read: which stages exist for a gem.
function_v0.name: list_gem_stages
